Open the PDF that matches your paper (US Letter or A4) and print at Actual size / 100% — turn off Fit, Shrink, or "fit to page." Portrait orientation. Letter 8×10 side margins are a little wider (about 6.35 mm) but still tight. If crop marks clip, use the trim rectangle as your guide, or print that page at a print shop.

results.title: Hanukkah Games Bundle: Printable Party Games for Family and Adults, Picture Bingo, Trivia, Dreidel Kit and Secret Mission
results.description:
Five printable Hanukkah party games in one download: picture bingo, a Hanukkah trivia quiz, a secret-mission party game, a dreidel kit with a paper dreidel to build, and latke-party place cards. Play one on a quiet family night or set them all out at your Hanukkah party. For families, friends, classrooms and office parties, ages 4 to adult (the trivia and secret missions suit ages 8 and up; the bingo has pictures with names for early readers).

WHAT'S INCLUDED (one PDF with everything, 80 pages)
1. PICTURE BINGO: 40 different 5x5 cards (one per page) with 36 Hanukkah pictures, each with its name: menorah, shamash, dreidel and its letters, latkes, sufganiyah, gelt and more. Plus 36 caller cards, a caller checklist and four ways to play.
2. SECRET MISSION, HANUKKAH EDITION: every guest gets a secret mission to complete at the party without being caught. 48 original mission cards and 6 blank cards, a 2-page host guide, table rules cards, card backs, Spy slips, a Score and Reveal sheet, award certificates and mission envelopes.
3. DREIDEL KIT: how to play dreidel, what the letters nun, gimel, hei and shin stand for (and the Israel version with pei), a score sheet with a no-tokens points game, and two paper dreidels to build (one with shin, one with pei).
4. HANUKKAH TRIVIA: 40 multiple-choice questions in four rounds (The Story, The Lights, Food and Fun, Dreidel and Words) plus 4 tie-breakers, as question cards with the answer printed upside down, a team answer sheet and an answer key with a short note for every answer.
5. LATKE PARTY: six fillable fold-over place cards and six food tents (Latkes, Applesauce, Sour Cream, Sufganiyot and two blank ones you can type on).
A contents page and PDF bookmarks show where each game starts, so you can print just one game.

WHY THE BINGO CARDS ARE DIFFERENT
Each card holds 24 of the 36 pictures in its own order. No two cards are the same, no two cards share a whole row, column or diagonal, and every picture appears on about the same number of cards. A computer program checked this, and checked it again by reading the cards back out of the finished PDFs.

THE PAPER DREIDEL
A cube with a pointed base that you cut, fold and glue from one page of cardstock, then spin on a short pencil pushed through the top. The measurements were checked in code (every glued edge meets its partner); it has not been test-built from a printed page, so please print one first to see how it goes with your cardstock.

FACTS AND RESPECT
Every fact in the set was checked against at least two reputable published sources (the sources are named in the file). Customs differ between families and communities, so the text says "many families" or "according to tradition" where they do. No blessings or prayers are printed. The set has not been reviewed by a rabbi or Jewish educator; if anything does not match your family's tradition, please send us a message.

FILES AND SIZES
- 4 PDF files, 80 pages each: US Letter (8.5 x 11 in) in full color, US Letter ink-saver, A4 (210 x 297 mm) in full color and A4 ink-saver
- Cards, place cards and the dreidel print at the same size on US Letter and A4

HOW TO PRINT
- Print at 100% / Actual Size (not "Fit to page")
- White cardstock (65-110 lb) is best for cards, place cards and the paper dreidel; regular paper is fine for guides, score sheets and bingo cards
- Cut along the dashed lines (cut lines and crop marks are printed on the pages)
- Print only the pages you need with your printer's page-range option
- The ink-saver files use outlines instead of color fills, so they use less ink

FILLABLE NAMES
Name lines can be typed in a free PDF reader such as Adobe Acrobat Reader, then printed. Some phone and browser viewers cannot fill in PDF forms: print the page and write by hand instead.
